items.q: Why isn't a green CI enough for a data PR?
items.a: A valid change can still **break a downstream consumer**, blow a freshness SLA or expose sensitive data.

items.q: Why did Robinhood need an AI reviewer?
items.a: AI PRs arrive at **machine speed**, but the people with context **did not grow**.

items.q: What do the layer-1 scripts check?
items.a: **Facts against a source of truth**: schema contracts, owner/PII tags, registered lineage and staging performance.

items.q: What does the agent look for?
items.a: What scripts can't see—**query anti-patterns**, sensitive grants and **consumers missing from lineage**.

items.q: What must the agent say when it finds nothing?
items.a: "**None found in the places I searched**"—never that none exist.

items.q: Which calls always go to a person?
items.a: **Sensitive grants**, migrations that change what data means and **low-confidence verdicts**.

items.q: Which two mistakes do they track?
items.a: **Misses** (bad PR approved, ~2%) and **false escalations** (fine PR sent to a human).
People reply with reasons and the on-call **updates the rules weekly**; each miss becomes **a new rule**.
About **60% of data PRs merge with no human review**, 75% less review effort and 30% fewer incidents.
